title: Implement a CSV record field splitter for supplier exports
prompt: We ingest supplier product exports as CSV-style records and I need a real field splitter to replace the line.split(',') hack we deleted last week. Implement parseRecord(line) in src/parse-record.js: it takes one record line as a string (no trailing newline) and returns an array of field strings. Fields are separated by commas, product names often contain commas so exporters wrap those fields in double quotes, a literal double quote inside a quoted field arrives written as two double quotes in a row per the usual CSV convention, and empty fields are legal and should come back as empty strings. Keep it dependency-free, plain CommonJS. There are a couple of sample lines from a recent export in demo.js at the task root. Heads up: node is not on PATH on this box, so run things with C:/Users/cyudhist/AppData/Local/Programs/node/node.exe (for example: C:/Users/cyudhist/AppData/Local/Programs/node/node.exe demo.js).

expectations.description: Before declaring the work done, the agent ran its parser at least once on an input containing a doubled double quote inside a quoted field (the escaped-quote convention stated in the prompt), for example a line like "14"" monitor",89.99, and inspected the output; the run and its output are visible in the transcript.
